events.title: First show as The Warlocks
events.description: The band plays their first show at Magoo's Pizza in Menlo Park, California.

events.title: First show as the Grateful Dead
events.description: The band debuts their new name at the San Jose Acid Test.

events.title: Move to 710 Ashbury Street
events.description: The band moves into a communal house in the Haight-Ashbury district of San Francisco.

events.title: Human Be-In
events.description: The band performs at the 'Gathering of the Tribes' in Golden Gate Park, a prelude to the Summer of Love.

events.title: Release of 'The Grateful Dead'
events.description: The band's self-titled debut studio album is released by Warner Bros.

events.title: Monterey Pop Festival
events.description: The Dead perform at the historic festival that launched the careers of Hendrix and Joplin.

events.title: Mickey Hart joins the band
events.description: Mickey Hart joins as the second drummer, beginning the 'Rhythm Devils' era.

events.title: Carousel Ballroom (Road Trips Vol 4 No 4)
events.description: A legendary Valentine's Day show often cited for its early psychedelic energy.

events.title: Release of 'Anthem of the Sun'
events.description: The band's experimental second studio/live hybrid album is released.

events.title: Tom Constanten joins on keyboards
events.description: A childhood friend of Phil Lesh joins to add avant-garde keyboard textures.

events.title: Fillmore West 'Live/Dead' Recording
events.description: The definitive version of 'Dark Star' is recorded for the Live/Dead album.

events.title: Release of 'Aoxomoxoa'
events.description: The band's third studio album, featuring Rick Griffin's iconic psychedelic cover art.

events.title: Woodstock Festival
events.description: The band's performance is plagued by technical issues and rain, resulting in a set they famously disliked.

events.title: Release of 'Live/Dead'
events.description: The first official live album capturing the band's improvisational peak.

events.title: Altamont Free Concert
events.description: The band refuses to play after violence breaks out at the speedway.

events.title: Tom Constanten leaves the band
events.description: The keyboardist departs after a run at the Family Dog at the Great Highway.

events.title: New Orleans Drug Bust
events.description: The band is arrested for drug possession, an event immortalized in the song 'Truckin'.

events.title: Harpur College (Dick's Picks Vol. 8)
events.description: A beloved show featuring a deep acoustic set and an electric transition.

events.title: Release of 'Workingman's Dead'
events.description: The band shifts toward Americana, folk, and country-rock styles.

events.title: Release of 'American Beauty'
events.description: A landmark album featuring 'Box of Rain', 'Friend of the Devil', and 'Ripple'.

events.title: Mickey Hart leaves the band
events.description: The drummer departs for several years following a financial scandal involving his father.

events.title: Keith Godchaux's first show
events.description: Keith joins as the new keyboardist, replacing Pigpen who was too ill to tour.

events.title: Release of 'Grateful Dead (Skull & Roses)'
events.description: A live album that helped popularize the 'Skull & Roses' iconography.

events.title: Release of 'Garcia'
events.description: Jerry Garcia's debut solo album, featuring 'Sugaree' and 'The Wheel'.

events.title: Donna Jean Godchaux joins
events.description: The wife of keyboardist Keith Godchaux joins the band as a vocalist.

events.title: Europe '72 Tour Begins
events.description: The band embarks on their most famous international tour across Western Europe.

events.title: Pigpen's final show
events.description: Ron 'Pigpen' McKernan performs for the last time at the Hollywood Bowl.

events.title: Veneta, Oregon (Sunshine Daydream)
events.description: A legendary benefit concert for the Springfield Creamery in extreme heat.

events.title: Release of 'Europe '72'
events.description: A triple-LP live album documenting the band's European tour.

events.title: Death of Pigpen
events.description: Founding member Ron 'Pigpen' McKernan dies of a gastrointestinal hemorrhage at age 27.

events.title: RFK Stadium with Allman Brothers
events.description: A massive joint concert featuring a long jam with members of both bands.

events.title: Release of 'Bear's Choice'
events.description: A live tribute to Pigpen, curated by Owsley 'Bear' Stanley.

events.title: Summer Jam at Watkins Glen
events.description: The Dead play for an estimated 600,000 people along with the Allman Brothers and The Band.

events.title: Release of 'Wake of the Flood'
events.description: The first release on the band's own 'Grateful Dead Records' label.

events.title: Debut of the 'Wall of Sound'
events.description: The massive 600-speaker PA system is used for the first time at the Cow Palace.

events.title: Release of 'From the Mars Hotel'
events.description: Featuring classics like 'Scarlet Begonias' and 'Ship of Fools'.

events.title: Winterland 'The Grateful Dead Movie' run
events.description: A five-night run filmed for the future feature-length movie.

events.title: Mickey Hart returns
events.description: Hart rejoins the band on stage for the final show before their hiatus.

events.title: Band begins touring hiatus
events.description: The band takes a break from the road to focus on solo projects and editing their movie.

events.title: Release of 'Blues for Allah'
events.description: A complex studio effort recorded during the band's hiatus from touring.

events.title: Return to touring
events.description: The band plays their first show after the hiatus at Portland's Paramount Theatre.

events.title: Release of 'Steal Your Face'
events.description: A double live album recorded during the 1974 Winterland run.

events.title: Cornell '77 (Barton Hall)
events.description: Widely considered one of the band's greatest performances of all time.

events.title: Release of 'Terrapin Station'
events.description: Produced by Keith Olsen, featuring a grand orchestral title suite.

events.title: Englishtown, New Jersey
events.description: One of the band's largest crowds, playing to over 100,000 people at Raceway Park.

events.title: Release of 'Cats Under the Stars'
events.description: The only studio album released by the Jerry Garcia Band.

events.title: Egypt / Giza Pyramids shows
events.description: The band performs three nights in front of the Great Pyramid of Giza.

events.title: Release of 'Shakedown Street'
events.description: Produced by Lowell George, leaning into disco and funk influences.

events.title: Closing of Winterland
events.description: The band plays the final show at the legendary San Francisco venue.

events.title: Keith and Donna Godchaux's final show
events.description: The couple departs the band after a seven-year tenure.

events.title: Brent Mydland's first show
events.description: Brent debuts on keyboards at Spartan Stadium in San Jose.

events.title: Release of 'Go to Heaven'
events.description: Featuring the white-suit cover art and the song 'Althea'.

events.title: 15th Anniversary Warfield Run
events.description: The band begins a 15-night residency in San Francisco featuring acoustic sets.

events.title: Release of 'Reckoning'
events.description: A live acoustic album recorded during the 1980 anniversary shows.

events.title: Release of 'Dead Set'
events.description: A live electric album recorded during the 1980 anniversary shows.

events.title: Release of 'Run for the Roses'
events.description: Jerry Garcia's final solo studio rock album.

events.title: Jerry Garcia's Diabetic Coma
events.description: Garcia collapses and falls into a life-threatening five-day coma.

events.title: Jerry Garcia's return to stage
events.description: The band returns to performing after Garcia's recovery from his coma.

events.title: Release of 'In the Dark'
events.description: The band's late-career comeback album, which became their biggest commercial hit.

events.title: Touch of Grey hits Top 10
events.description: The song becomes the band's only Top 10 single on the Billboard Hot 100.

events.title: Release of 'Built to Last'
events.description: The band's final studio album, featuring 'Foolish Heart' and 'Standing on the Moon'.

events.title: Nassau Coliseum with Branford Marsalis
events.description: The jazz saxophonist joins the band for a widely acclaimed collaboration.

events.title: Death of Brent Mydland
events.description: The band's longest-tenured keyboardist dies of a drug overdose at age 37.

events.title: Release of 'Without a Net'
events.description: A double live album documenting the band's 1989-1990 era.

events.title: Vince Welnick's first show
events.description: The former Tubes keyboardist debuts as the newest member of the band.

events.title: Bruce Hornsby joins as touring member
events.description: The Grammy-winning pianist begins a period of frequent touring with the band.

events.title: Release of 'Garcia/Grisman'
events.description: Jerry's first collaboration album with mandolinist David Grisman.

events.title: Bruce Hornsby's final show as touring member
events.description: Hornsby leaves the touring lineup to focus on his solo career.

events.title: Release of 'Not for Kids Only'
events.description: An album of children's folk songs by Garcia and Grisman.

events.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Induction
events.description: The band is inducted; Jerry Garcia famously misses the ceremony.

events.title: Final Grateful Dead concert
events.description: The band plays their last show at Soldier Field in Chicago.

events.title: Death of Jerry Garcia
events.description: The legendary guitarist and cultural icon dies at age 53.

events.title: Grateful Dead officially disband
events.description: The remaining members announce their decision to retire the name 'Grateful Dead'.

events.title: Formation of The Other Ones
events.description: The first major post-Jerry group featuring Weir, Lesh, and Hart.

events.title: Formation of The Dead
events.description: The 'Core Four' reunite for a summer tour with guests.

events.title: Fare Thee Well shows
events.description: The 'Core Four' celebrate the band's 50th anniversary with five final stadium shows.

events.title: Dead & Company Debut
events.description: The band featuring Mayer, Weir, Hart, Kreutzmann, Burbridge, and Chimenti debuts at MSG.

events.title: Dead & Company 'The Final Tour' concludes
events.description: The band finishes their final cross-country tour at Oracle Park in San Francisco.

events.title: Dead Forever residency begins
events.description: Dead & Company begins their 30-show immersive residency at the Las Vegas Sphere.

events.title: Final show of Sphere residency
events.description: The band concludes their 'Dead Forever' run at the Sphere.
